{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Interface Licence Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (for Mortgage Logic.com — "Client") 
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings and recommended positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Of the eighteen rules assessed, **six require negotiation** (two critical, three high, one medium) and **two clauses are missing entirely**. The remaining ten items are compliant, several of them because the Agreement is either silent in our favour or contains vendor-side commitments that run to our benefit.

The commercial risk is concentrated in the **risk-allocation architecture of Section 12**. The Agreement caps TrueLink's liability at twelve months' hosting and support compensation while leaving our own liability — including under a very broad indemnity covering Client breach, the Web Site, Client Content and third-party injury — entirely uncapped, with no mutual exclusion of indirect or consequential damages anywhere in the document. That asymmetry is squarely within walk-away territory under our playbook. Compounding this, TrueLink's indemnity is limited to breach of contract: there is **no third-party IP infringement indemnity and no non-infringement warranty** on which a breach-based indemnity could operate.

Three further structural gaps warrant attention. First, **ownership**: the Agreement confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface but says nothing about our ownership of Client Content, Client Intellectual Property, our borrower and loan data, or the Support Services work product we pay for. Second, **insurance**: the word does not appear in the document, notwithstanding that TrueLink hosts our web site, Client Content and customer credit data. Third, **exit**: there is no transition assistance or data return obligation — Section 13 places the migration burden on us (30 days for a new name server, 60 days for new hosting) with no corresponding duty on TrueLink to assist or to return our data.

On the positive side, the Agreement is genuinely clean on several fronts we would ordinarily have to fight for: **no exclusivity, no non-compete, no non-solicit, no MFN burdening us, no audit rights against us, and no liquidated damages or termination fees**. Section 2(a) affirmatively preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or license competing software and services. Section 14 gives us an at-will termination right, Section 13 renews in one-year increments on 30 days' notice, and Section 6 gives us a vendor-side most-favoured-rate commitment and a one-year price freeze. California law and California courts sit at our accepted fallback. We recommend we do not disturb any of these.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 12 Indemnity |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 12 Indemnity |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 12 Indemnity |
| 4 | High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 2 Licence |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Licence |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Licence |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 2 Licence |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 Covenants and Warranties of Client |
| 11 | Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 12 Indemnity |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 12 Indemnity |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 Compensation |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 Compensation |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant (at fallback) | § 5 Compensation |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 Covenants and Warranties of Client |
| 18 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity |

### 2.1 Deviations and gaps — what we changed and why

**INDEMN (critical).** Section 12(b) gives us only a breach-of-contract indemnity, covering "any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations." There is no third-party IP infringement indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, and no TrueLink non-infringement warranty for a breach-based indemnity to bite on — Section 2 addresses only TrueLink's own IP rights and our domain-name searches, and Section 12's disclaimer strips implied warranties. Our playbook fallback requires a vendor IP indemnity, so this fails even the fallback. The imbalance is aggravated by the breadth of the Client indemnity in 12(a). *Redline:* expand TrueLink's indemnity to cover third-party IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorised access to Client Content, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, plus standard notice, control and cooperation procedure. We left our own indemnity in place as the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position on vendor coverage.

**LOL-CAP (critical).** The only liability limitation, buried at the end of Section 12, caps TrueLink alone at twelve months' hosting and support compensation and is further narrowed to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 only; our liability is uncapped. There is no mutual exclusion of indirect or consequential damages. Our fallback requires a mutual twelve-month fee cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. *Redline:* make the cap mutual and of general application at the greater of twelve months' compensation and USD 1,000,000, add an Excluded Claims carve-out (confidentiality and data security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and confirm our payment obligations sit outside the limitation.

**ASSIGN (high).** Section 15 is the only assignment provision and there is no change-of-control language in the document. The clause is mutual and carves out affiliates, but it fails the fallback on two material terms: there is no successor/M&A carve-out, so any merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all our assets requires TrueLink's approval; and approval is absolute rather than subject to a "not unreasonably withheld" standard, so TrueLink could block a corporate transaction outright. *Redline:* add an affiliate/successor carve-out for Client on written notice, apply a reasonableness standard to consent, bar assignment by TrueLink to a Client competitor, and confirm a change of control of Client is neither an assignment nor a termination or re-pricing trigger.

**IP (high).** Section 2(d) confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface, which is acceptable, but nothing confirms that we retain ownership of Client Content, Client Intellectual Property or our borrower and loan data, and nothing addresses ownership of or a licence to the Section 4 Support Services work product. Section 13's statement that we "shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content" on discontinuation of Hosting Service is incidental, and Section 10 treats our Intellectual Property and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" as Proprietary Information for confidentiality purposes only — which is not an ownership or licence grant. *Redline:* insert a reciprocal Client ownership provision immediately after the existing Ownership clause (assignment of Work Product, licence back for embedded TrueLink IP, no joint ownership). Noted but not separately redlined: Section 8(d)'s licence to exploit "Credit Data" is a term-limited licence over narrowly defined raw third-party data, archived and not combined with Client Proprietary Information and subject to the Non-Competition Agreement — within the negotiated bargain rather than an assignment of our data.

**LICENSE (high).** The Section 2(a) grant runs to "Client" alone; our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not licensed, and the Exhibit A site-amendment right in Section 2(b)(ii) covers locations only, not additional licensed entities. That fails the fallback of affiliate coverage on written notice. Section 15 also requires consent for any transfer other than to a financially responsible affiliate, so the licence is not transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction as the fallback requires. The licence is not revocable at TrueLink's discretion — Section 2(c) ties it to the term and the Section 13 cut-offs are breach-based — so this is a deviation rather than a walk-away. *Redline:* extend the grant to our affiliates and contractors and add mutual successor-transfer rights.

**WARRANTY (medium).** TrueLink's only express warranty (Section 9) is a Y2K date-processing warranty. There is no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no professional or workmanlike services warranty, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair, replace, refund or re-performance remedy. Section 11's "same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" is a self-referential standard of care, not a warranty with a remedy, and the disclaimer — while carving out express warranties — leaves nothing meaningful behind. This fails the fallback of 90 days software / 30 days services with remedies. *Redline:* insert an express performance and conformance warranty at the preferred position (12 months software, workmanlike services, no malicious code, compliance with laws) with a repair, replace or refund remedy; the fallback period is negotiable.

**INSURANCE (missing).** A full-text search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the miscellaneous provisions contain no coverage requirement. TrueLink hosts our web site, Client Content and customer credit data. *Redline:* new Section 31 after Force Majeure at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O including tech E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request — with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) flagged in the comment. The survival clause references "Sections 1 and 5 through 30"; a conforming cross-reference update can be handled administratively.

**TRANSITION (missing).** Section 14 fixes only the date services stop. Section 13 puts the burden on us to arrange a new name server within 30 days and new hosting within 60 days, with no TrueLink obligation to assist with migration or to return Client Content, Credit Data or other Client data. Section 10 has no return-or-destroy mechanic and Section 2(f) addresses only TrueLink's own backup practices. Nothing reaches even the fallback of 90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days. *Redline:* insert into Section 14 six months' assistance at then-current rates, return in machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification, carved out for legally required retention. The insertion sits in a surviving section under Section 24.

### 2.2 Compliant items — noted, not redlined

- **MINCOMMIT** sits at the fallback and is not redlined: Section 5(a)'s monthly minimum is confined to the current 12-month term, we hold an at-will termination right under Section 14, and there is no shortfall penalty, make-whole or acceleration of unused minimums. Two drafting points: the minimum dollar amounts remain blank (`$____`) and should be completed with figures reflecting realistic baseline usage before signature; and Section 6 carves the minimum monthly fees out of both our right to supporting documentation and our right to contest charges.
- **RENEWAL** meets the preferred position on renewal length (one year) and customer opt-out (30 days). Short of ideal drafting, and available as goodwill asks if renewal economics are negotiated: no vendor reminder 60 days before renewal, and no CPI/3% cap on renewal pricing, since Section 6 freezes Hosting Services costs for year one only.
- **T4C** meets the preferred position on both material terms. Noted: no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (largely moot, as Section 5(a) bills monthly with invoices paid 15 days after receipt, i.e. in arrears), and end-of-term non-renewal notice is 30 rather than 90 days — mutual, operating only at natural expiry, and shortening it would cut back our own flexibility. **Section 14 is expressed as "Subject to Section 4 hereof," and Section 4 is not in the reviewed text**; cross-references in Sections 5 and 6 indicate Section 4 concerns minimum monthly fees rather than any limit on our termination right, but this must be confirmed on receipt of the full Section 4.
- **EXCLUSIVITY / NONCOMPETE.** Section 2(a) is non-exclusive and affirmatively confirms we may acquire, develop or licence competing software and services. Noted for commercial awareness only: Section 3(i) requires us to order a TrueLink credit report on each borrower for which underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface — a narrow, channel-tied service requirement, not exclusive dealing. The separate **Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in Section 8(d) limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data (i.e. runs in our favour) but is not before us and should be reviewed independently.
- **AUDIT.** Silence is better than our preferred position; we should not introduce an audit right against ourselves. Verification mechanics run our way (Section 6 documentation and contest rights; Section 3(e) real-time usage statistics and raw log files).
- **GOVLAW.** California law and exclusive venue in San Luis Obispo County sit at our fallback, with no arbitration provision. Venue in TrueLink's local county rather than New York County is noted, not redlined.
- **MFN / NOSOLICIT / LD.** No customer-side parity undertaking, no non-solicit or no-hire covenant, and no liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination charge.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following must be resolved before we can recommend signature:

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped Vendor (LOL-CAP, § 12).** Our playbook identifies "Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped" as a walk-away. A mutual cap with the Excluded Claims carve-out, and a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages, is non-negotiable.
2. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE).** The absence of any coverage requirement for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory under the rule. We require at minimum the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
3. **No IP infringement indemnity (INDEMN, § 12).** The vendor indemnity fails even the fallback. Given the absence of any non-infringement warranty, we carry undiluted infringement exposure on a licensed Interface.
4. **Approaching walk-away — assignment consent with no M&A carve-out (ASSIGN, § 15).** An absolute consent right over our merger, acquisition or asset sale approaches the walk-away case of a consent requirement on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six deviations and two missing clauses (INDEMN, LOL-CAP, ASSIGN, IP, LICENSE, WARRANTY, INSURANCE, TRANSITION), holding the four walk-away items as conditions of signature and signalling the stated fallbacks on warranty duration and insurance limits.
2. **Request the missing Section 4** and confirm that the "Subject to Section 4" qualifier in Section 14 does not constrain our at-will termination right.
3. **Obtain and review the separate Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in Section 8(d), which is not before us.
4. **Commercial team to complete the blank minimum monthly amounts** in Section 5(a) and Section 6 with figures reflecting realistic baseline usage, and consider whether to press Section 6 to extend documentation and contest rights to the minimum fees.
5. **Optional goodwill asks** if renewal economics reopen: a 60-day vendor renewal reminder and a CPI/3% cap on post-year-one uplifts.
6. **Administrative conform** of the survival cross-reference ("Sections 1 and 5 through 30") once the new insurance section is added.

*We recommend we do not reopen the exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, audit, liquidated damages, governing law, renewal or termination-for-convenience provisions, each of which meets or exceeds our position.*"}
